front: What are the four broad layers in a typical database request path?
back: Transport, query processing, execution, and storage.
accepted_answers: Transport, query processing, execution, and storage.
hint: Follow a query from the client toward disk.

front: A query reaches a database node. What does the query processor do before execution begins?
back: It parses, validates, and interprets the query, then helps produce a plan the execution layer can run.
accepted_answers: It parses, validates, and interprets the query, then helps produce a plan the execution layer can run.
hint: This happens before local or remote operators execute.

front: Why can two database systems with similar SQL syntax behave very differently in production?
back: Their storage engines, concurrency control, recovery, replication, and distribution choices can have very different trade-offs.
accepted_answers: Their storage engines, concurrency control, recovery, replication, and distribution choices can have very different trade-offs.
hint: Look below the query language.

front: What is the storage engine responsible for?
back: It stores, retrieves, and manages records in memory and on persistent media, exposing low-level access operations to higher database layers.
accepted_answers: It stores, retrieves, and manages records in memory and on persistent media, exposing low-level access operations to higher database layers.
hint: Think of the component below SQL and schemas.

front: How do the transaction manager and lock manager contribute to correctness?
back: They coordinate concurrent work so transactions preserve logical consistency and physical data integrity.
accepted_answers: They coordinate concurrent work so transactions preserve logical consistency and physical data integrity.
hint: Separate transaction scheduling from object protection.

front: What is the primary workload difference between OLTP and OLAP?
back: OLTP handles many short operational transactions; OLAP handles longer analytical scans and aggregations.
accepted_answers: OLTP handles many short operational transactions; OLAP handles longer analytical scans and aggregations.
hint: Operational requests versus analytical questions.

front: When is an HTAP system attractive?
back: When a workload needs both transactional updates and near-real-time analytical queries without maintaining completely separate systems.
accepted_answers: When a workload needs both transactional updates and near-real-time analytical queries without maintaining completely separate systems.
hint: It combines two workload families.

front: Why should database selection start with access patterns rather than popularity rankings?
back: A database is suitable only if its query types, data size, read-write ratio, latency, consistency, and operational behavior match the real workload.
accepted_answers: A database is suitable only if its query types, data size, read-write ratio, latency, consistency, and operational behavior match the real workload.
hint: The best database is workload-dependent.

front: A benchmark shows one database winning on a laptop. Why is that insufficient for a production decision?
back: Short synthetic tests may hide scale, durability, compaction, failover, and operational costs; realistic long-running workloads are needed.
accepted_answers: Short synthetic tests may hide scale, durability, compaction, failover, and operational costs; realistic long-running workloads are needed.
hint: Ask what the benchmark omitted.

front: Why is a slower durable database often preferable to a faster database that risks losing data?
back: Performance is useful only after correctness and durability requirements are met; lost data creates larger business risk than moderate latency.
accepted_answers: Performance is useful only after correctness and durability requirements are met; lost data creates larger business risk than moderate latency.
hint: Reliability is a constraint, not a bonus.

front: How does a row-oriented layout improve an OLTP read that fetches an entire customer record?
back: Fields from the same row are stored near each other, so the database can retrieve the record with good spatial locality.
accepted_answers: Fields from the same row are stored near each other, so the database can retrieve the record with good spatial locality.
hint: Most columns of one row are consumed together.

front: Why can a row store waste I/O on a query that scans one column across millions of rows?
back: Blocks also contain unneeded columns, so the engine reads and discards data that the query did not request.
accepted_answers: Blocks also contain unneeded columns, so the engine reads and discards data that the query did not request.
hint: The physical unit is wider than the projection.

front: Why are column-oriented layouts effective for analytical aggregation?
back: Values of one column are stored together, improving scan locality, compression, and vectorized processing over many rows.
accepted_answers: Values of one column are stored together, improving scan locality, compression, and vectorized processing over many rows.
hint: Think same type, contiguous values.

front: A service repeatedly reads full orders by primary key. Which layout is usually the better starting point and why?
back: A row-oriented layout, because point lookups usually consume most fields of one record together.
accepted_answers: A row-oriented layout, because point lookups usually consume most fields of one record together.
hint: Match physical locality to the read shape.

front: An analytics job computes averages over three columns in a 100-column table. Which layout is usually favorable?
back: A column-oriented layout, because it can scan only the requested columns instead of loading entire rows.
accepted_answers: A column-oriented layout, because it can scan only the requested columns instead of loading entire rows.
hint: The projection is narrow but the row count is large.

front: Why is a wide-column store not the same as a columnar analytical database?
back: A wide-column store organizes rows by key and groups related columns into families, while a columnar analytical store physically groups values by column for scans.
accepted_answers: A wide-column store organizes rows by key and groups related columns into families, while a columnar analytical store physically groups values by column for scans.
hint: Similar name, different physical purpose.

front: What is a heap file?
back: A data file whose records are not maintained in key order, commonly appended in write order.
accepted_answers: A data file whose records are not maintained in key order, commonly appended in write order.
hint: Fast placement, separate lookup structure.

front: What trade-off does a heap file make?
back: It makes insertion simple and cheap, but efficient lookup normally requires a separate index that points to record locations.
accepted_answers: It makes insertion simple and cheap, but efficient lookup normally requires a separate index that points to record locations.
hint: Writes are easy; search needs help.

front: How does a hash-organized file locate a record?
back: It hashes the key to choose a bucket, then searches within that bucket.
accepted_answers: It hashes the key to choose a bucket, then searches within that bucket.
hint: The key determines a bucket.

front: Why are hash-organized files weak for range scans?
back: Hashing destroys key order, so nearby key values are not necessarily stored near one another.
accepted_answers: Hashing destroys key order, so nearby key values are not necessarily stored near one another.
hint: Equality is natural; ordering is not.

front: What is an index-organized table?
back: A structure that stores the full data records inside the primary index in key order.
accepted_answers: A structure that stores the full data records inside the primary index in key order.
hint: The index is also the data file.

front: What I/O advantage can an index-organized table provide?
back: After locating a key in the index, the engine already has the record and avoids another lookup into a separate heap file.
accepted_answers: After locating a key in the index, the engine already has the record and avoids another lookup into a separate heap file.
hint: Remove one indirection.

front: What distinguishes a clustered index from a nonclustered index?
back: A clustered index follows the physical order of the data; a nonclustered index points to data stored in a different order.
accepted_answers: A clustered index follows the physical order of the data; a nonclustered index points to data stored in a different order.
hint: Compare index key order with record order.

front: Why can a table have many secondary indexes but only one physical clustering order?
back: Each secondary index can provide a different logical lookup path, but the records can be physically ordered only one way at a time.
accepted_answers: Each secondary index can provide a different logical lookup path, but the records can be physically ordered only one way at a time.
hint: Many maps, one physical arrangement.

front: What is the benefit of a secondary index storing the primary key instead of a raw file offset?
back: Record movement changes only the primary structure; secondary entries remain valid because they resolve through the stable primary key.
accepted_answers: Record movement changes only the primary structure; secondary entries remain valid because they resolve through the stable primary key.
hint: An extra lookup can buy easier maintenance.

front: What is the cost of routing secondary lookups through the primary index?
back: It adds an extra indirection and potentially another cache miss or I/O before reaching the record.
accepted_answers: It adds an extra indirection and potentially another cache miss or I/O before reaching the record.
hint: Stability is not free.

front: What three properties are useful for comparing storage structures?
back: Buffering, immutability, and ordering.
accepted_answers: Buffering, immutability, and ordering.
hint: The book uses these repeatedly.

front: How does buffering improve write performance?
back: It groups multiple small updates so the storage engine can apply them in larger, more efficient batches.
accepted_answers: It groups multiple small updates so the storage engine can apply them in larger, more efficient batches.
hint: Amortize expensive work.

front: What does immutability mean for an on-disk storage component?
back: Once written, the component is not modified in place; updates create new records, pages, or files.
accepted_answers: Once written, the component is not modified in place; updates create new records, pages, or files.
hint: New state is written elsewhere.

front: What maintenance cost often accompanies immutable storage?
back: Old and new versions must later be merged or garbage-collected, deferring work to compaction or cleanup.
accepted_answers: Old and new versions must later be merged or garbage-collected, deferring work to compaction or cleanup.
hint: Cheap foreground writes create background work.

front: Why is key ordering valuable on disk?
back: Nearby keys can be scanned sequentially, enabling efficient range queries and predictable traversal.
accepted_answers: Nearby keys can be scanned sequentially, enabling efficient range queries and predictable traversal.
hint: Ordering benefits more than equality lookup.

front: Why might a storage engine intentionally write data out of key order?
back: Appending in arrival order can reduce random writes and improve ingestion throughput, with ordering work deferred to indexes or compaction.
accepted_answers: Appending in arrival order can reduce random writes and improve ingestion throughput, with ordering work deferred to indexes or compaction.
hint: Optimize the write path first.

front: Why do database file formats need explicit byte order and type encoding?
back: Raw bytes have no inherent meaning; stable encoding lets data be interpreted consistently across processes, platforms, and versions.
accepted_answers: Raw bytes have no inherent meaning; stable encoding lets data be interpreted consistently across processes, platforms, and versions.
hint: Persistence outlives one process.

front: What problem does a slotted page solve?
back: It lets variable-size records move inside a page while external references use stable slot identifiers rather than raw byte offsets.
accepted_answers: It lets variable-size records move inside a page while external references use stable slot identifiers rather than raw byte offsets.
hint: Separate logical record identity from physical position.

front: How can a slotted page preserve key order without physically rewriting every record?
back: It can sort the slot directory while leaving record bodies in convenient locations within the page.
accepted_answers: It can sort the slot directory while leaving record bodies in convenient locations within the page.
hint: Order pointers instead of payloads.

front: Why does a page header commonly include a magic number and format version?
back: They let the reader verify the page type and select the correct decoding logic before trusting the remaining bytes.
accepted_answers: They let the reader verify the page type and select the correct decoding logic before trusting the remaining bytes.
hint: Identify and interpret the page safely.

front: What is the purpose of a page checksum?
back: It detects accidental corruption by recomputing a digest when the page is read and comparing it with the stored value.
accepted_answers: It detects accidental corruption by recomputing a digest when the page is read and comparing it with the stored value.
hint: Integrity against unintended changes.

front: Why is a CRC not an authentication mechanism?
back: It detects accidental errors but is not designed to resist an attacker who deliberately changes data and recomputes the value.
accepted_answers: It detects accidental errors but is not designed to resist an attacker who deliberately changes data and recomputes the value.
hint: Corruption detection is not tamper resistance.

front: A database upgrade changes the page layout. What compatibility mechanism is required?
back: The system needs versioned readers, migration logic, or a stable header that identifies the old format so pages can be interpreted safely.
accepted_answers: The system needs versioned readers, migration logic, or a stable header that identifies the old format so pages can be interpreted safely.
hint: Old bytes must remain understandable.
